html:
The Comoros, especially Anjouan, is one of the world's main producers of ylang-ylang oil, distilled from the flowers of a tropical tree and used in perfumes such as Chanel No. 5.

The tree came from Southeast Asia, and French planters spread it in the Comoros, Mayotte and Madagascar in the early 20th century. Flowers are picked by hand at dawn and distilled in small family stills, burning large amounts of firewood.

With vanilla and cloves, ylang-ylang is one of the islands' few exports, so world perfume prices matter greatly to farmers. The trade links Anjouan to French perfumers and to the spice crops of Madagascar.
